description: looking for: Teammates who are curious, collaborative, willing to learn, and serious about building a technically sound solution. Experience in Python, data science, statistics, geospatial analysis/GIS, satellite data, machine learning, backend development, or UI/UX would be valuable.
summary:
Fireline is a browser-based tool for exploring wildfire activity across time and place. Its data pipeline is designed to process NASA FIRMS active-fire records from the MODIS and VIIRS satellite instruments, normalize their fields, filter records by confidence, and group detections into approximate spatial cell-days. It also preserves satellite platform details and estimates scaling factors from dates when both sensors observed fires.

The web app brings fire activity into an interactive map and historical calendar. Users can select countries, filter by year, month, or sensor, inspect hotspot details, compare activity with historical monthly patterns, explore regional subdivisions, pin fires for side-by-side comparison, and download filtered data as CSV.

By making a large dataset easier to explore in a browser, Fireline aims to help researchers, students, and planners find patterns worth investigating. It is an analysis and exploration tool, not a live alert service or fire-spread forecast.
details:
Fireline is a browser-based wildfire activity explorer built around a Python data-processing pipeline and an interactive web app. The pipeline uses DuckDB to scan FIRMS CSV files from disk, normalize MODIS and VIIRS fields, apply confidence filters, map detections to approximate spatial cells and UTC dates, and keep one strongest observation per cell-day. It retains the sensor and satellite platform provenance and estimates provisional VIIRS scaling from overlapping MODIS and VIIRS records. These scaling factors depend on the supplied archive and are not presented as a peer-reviewed global calibration.

In the app, users can select a country, filter activity by year, month, and sensor, view mapped hotspots, explore a year-by-month calendar, draw or enter an area of interest, inspect hotspot details, compare pinned fires, review historical monthly anomalies, and export filtered records as CSV. The interface is built with React, JavaScript, and Vite; MapLibre GL JS provides the map. Python and DuckDB support the data pipeline.

Fireline is designed to make satellite fire records easier to explore without requiring desktop GIS software. Its intended value is to help researchers, students, and planners identify patterns for further investigation. It is not a real-time monitoring or alert system, and its comparisons depend on the coverage and quality of the data provided.

Data-status sentence: Fireline uses NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS NOAA-20 active-fire data covering 2018–2025. The data is processed into pre-aggregated analytics for the app; the raw source CSV files are not included in the repository.
